name: SF Fin
description: Connect SF Pi to a Fin (formerly Intercom) workspace: Pi-owned masked credentials, Guardrail-mediated Fin CLI install, doctor and debug, Fin-as-code authoring (procedures, simulations, guidance, data connectors), a CLI vs MCP surface comparison, and a Fin Agent API test harness.

docs.summary: Provides Pi-native `/login sf-fin`, which asks for the workspace hosting region and collects a Fin personal API token through SF Pi's shared fixed-mask input. Pi alone persists it. The `sf_fin` family tool and `/sf-fin` command expose cached status; a live read-only doctor (Node, Fin CLI presence and version freshness, credential, workspace identity through `intercom me`); Fin CLI install/update through exactly pinned global npm (TUI confirmation for humans, SF Guardrail mediation in the `fin` Power Tool family for the agent); and a redacted debug bundle with optional one-shot verbose traces. The CLI always runs with the token in the child-process environment only and an SF Pi-private CLI config directory. `/sf-pi doctor` receives cached-only checks.
stateFiles: ~/.pi/agent/auth.json entries: sf-fin / sf-fin-<workspace> (personal API token plus credential.env.INTERCOM_REGION), sf-fin-agent / sf-fin-agent-<workspace> (Fin Agent API key), and sf-fin-browser / sf-fin-browser-<workspace> (Fin admin sign-in cookies)
<globalAgentDir>/sf-pi/sf-fin/workspaces.json (named workspace profiles: kind, verified app id and region; shared read-only with SF Guardrail; no credentials)
<globalAgentDir>/sf-pi/sf-fin/agent-api-status.json (last Fin Agent API access outcome; no key material)
<globalAgentDir>/sf-pi/sf-fin/sdk/<app id>/ (owner-only Fin SDK download and extraction)
safety: Interactive `/login sf-fin` masks the personal API token through SF Pi's shared credential input and returns it to Pi under provider id `sf-fin`; SF Fin writes no second secret store.

The token reaches the Fin CLI only through an allowlisted child-process environment, never argv, and the child uses an SF Pi-private `INTERCOM_CONFIG_DIR`, so the user's own CLI keychain entry and `~/.intercom` files are never read or written.
CLI output is scrubbed of the token before it reaches status, tool results, or logs; status files store only non-secret workspace identity and install readiness.

Doctor runs `intercom --version` and `intercom me` only; Fin SDK actions enable the SDK by default on first use through an explicit probe → POST /fin-sdk/enable → verify sequence before any `fin …` CLI call, so the CLI's silent auto-enable never fires; the `/sf-pi doctor` provider reads cached state only.

Install runs exactly `npm install -g @intercom/cli@<exact version>` without sudo or `@latest`, honors npm release-age policy, and refuses CLIs not installed by global npm; agent execution (`allow_mutation=true`) is an SF Guardrail native mutation in the `fin` Power Tool family.
Verbose traces drop Authorization, Cookie, and bearer/basic values, are written as 0600 files with ten-file retention, self-disarm after the armed runs, and expose only the file path to the model.

Procedure upload validates against the workspace schema first, never sets state (cannot publish), and verifies the saved copy semantically; simulation sets are validated per test; upload, upload_simulations, and simulate are SF Guardrail native writes in the fin Power Tool family, and validate is local.

Fin simulates live procedures only; sdk simulate warns on drafts. sdk publish|pause plans by default; allow_mutation=true executes as the exact SF Guardrail mutation native-sf-fin-procedure-state (never session-approved) and verifies the resulting state.

Fin simulates live procedures only; sdk simulate warns on drafts. sdk publish|pause plans by default; allow_mutation=true executes as the exact SF Guardrail mutation native-sf-fin-procedure-state (never session-approved) and verifies the resulting state.

Guidance uploads are always paused and data connectors only as drafts; sdk guidance_state plans by default and executes as the exact SF Guardrail mutation native-sf-fin-procedure-state. The Fin Agent API key is a separate Pi provider (sf-fin-agent), sent only as an HTTPS Authorization header; agent run is native-sf-fin-agent-run because resolved conversations are billable. surfaces runs only local --help commands.

The Fin Agent API key is rejected at login when it is malformed or equals the personal token, and every Agent API request refuses a key equal to the active personal token (constant-time digest comparison); it is sent only as an HTTPS Authorization header to the fixed regional host with redirects refused.

Personal-token login detects the region from /me on the fixed regional hosts and refuses a token every region rejects. Named workspaces have their own Pi sign-ins; environment fallbacks apply only to the default workspace. Setup binds a workspace to the app id its token proves and refuses a different app. SF Guardrail treats a prod (or unknown) Fin workspace like a production org: no session approvals, and Power Tool Mode needs the production opt-in.

Fin admin pages (/sf-fin admin) open only verified pages for the workspace's verified app id in the shared SF Pi browser and navigate and read only. Sign-in is human-only in a visible window, with owner-only saved-login files. All browser text is masked, and pages that can show a key get no screenshots or editor reads. A committing click there is bound to the Fin workspace in SF Guardrail and is never session-approved.

The Fin admin sign-in (/login sf-fin-browser) is two Fin cookies persisted by Pi. They are restored into the shared browser only for one admin action and removed afterwards, so the browser's own state file never keeps them. Values go to the browser on stdin, never on a command line. Pi reports the sign-in as expired when Fin's remember cookie expires (about two weeks).
